claims.claim: Temporal databases have long distinguished valid time, when something holds in the represented world, from transaction time, when it is recorded in the database. These are established data-management concepts, although their application to a conversational persona requires additional decisions about evidence and interpretation. [FN02]

claims.claim: Appraisal models begin with a more structured question: how does the represented event relate to goals, expectations, responsibility and available responses? The model is a computational account with explicit theoretical assumptions, including the relationship between appraisal and emotion; it is not a settled description of every human emotional process. claims.claim: A timestamp tells us when a clock said an event occurred. It does not automatically tell us what another process had observed. Its central distinction remains useful here: events can have an order through communication and dependency that cannot be recovered simply by reading wall-clock labels. [R4B06]
